fields.name: Ledger
fields.description: A plain-text budgeting tool that turns bank exports into a monthly picture in one command.

fields.audience: Anyone who keeps a budget in a spreadsheet and dreads the monthly paste
fields.problem: Every bank exports a different CSV, so reconciling takes an evening.
fields.goal: One command that normalises any export and prints a clean monthly summary.

fields.ownership: Built the parser, the rules engine and the report.

fields.approach: Describe each bank once in a small config file, then pipe any export through it.
fields.tools: Rust, a hand-written CSV adapter layer, golden-file tests.
fields.decisions:
Plain-text files over a database, so the data outlives the tool.
Rules are ordered and readable, not learned.

fields.challenge: Banks change their export format without warning.
fields.solution: Fail loudly with the exact line and column, and ship a fixture test per bank.
fields.tradeoff: More upfront config per bank, but no silent miscategorisation.

fields.result: Twelve months of exports from four banks reconcile to the cent.
fields.evidence: Golden tests for every adapter, plus a manual check against statement totals.
fields.limitations: Only tested on checking and credit card exports.

fields.learned: Golden-file tests made every refactor safe.
fields.next_steps: A forecast view and recurring-payment detection.
